sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我曾在凌晨4点半给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Vivian Yee, filling in as hoSt.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Vivian Yee，代班主持。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: For weeks, thousands of high school students in France have been out in the streets protesting the conditions in public schools.
sentences.zh: 几周以来，法国成千上万的高中生走上街头，抗议公立学校的现状。

sentences.en: Yesterday's protest drew in more than 250,000 people.
sentences.zh: 昨天的抗议活动吸引了超过25万人参加。

sentences.en: Since they began last month, more than 6,000 arrested.
sentences.zh: 自上个月抗议开始以来，已有超过6000人被捕。

sentences.en: Some protesters set fires and clashed with riot police.
sentences.zh: 一些抗议者纵火并与防暴警察发生冲突。

sentences.en: Several hundred teenagers have been injured, prompting authorities to suspend the use of stun grenades.
sentences.zh: 数百名青少年受伤，促使当局暂停使用眩晕弹。

sentences.en: One thing they want is for the government to spend more on schools.
sentences.zh: 他们的诉求之一是希望政府增加对学校的投入。

sentences.en: Some schools don't have chairs.
sentences.zh: 有些学校没有椅子。

sentences.en: Some schools don't have tables.
sentences.zh: 有些学校没有桌子。

sentences.en: There are rats in the kitchens.
sentences.zh: 厨房里有老鼠。

sentences.en: A lot of schools, they don't have enough teachers.
sentences.zh: 很多学校的老师都不够。

sentences.en: Teachers are often not here.
sentences.zh: 老师经常不在岗。

sentences.en: Like, my brother, he's had, like, no class.
sentences.zh: 比如我弟弟，他几乎没上过课。

sentences.en: But with the current state of French finances, that won't be easy.
sentences.zh: 但以法国目前的财政状况，这并不容易实现。

sentences.en: Because after years of overspending,
sentences.zh: 因为在经历了多年的过度支出后，

sentences.en: France is in crisis and driving toward a fiscal cliff.
sentences.zh: 法国正处于危机之中，正驶向财政悬崖。

sentences.en: Today, Times Paris Bureau Chief Mark Landler on whether France's long struggle to fund its generous welfare state is finally reaching a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 今天，本报巴黎分社社长Mark Landler将探讨法国为维持其慷慨福利国家制度所做的长期斗争是否终于到了临界点。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 9th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月9日，星期五。

sentences.en: Mark Landler, Paris Bureau Chief, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 巴黎分社社长Mark Landler，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: It's great to be here, Vivian.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，Vivian。

sentences.en: Mark, we know, and you know, from covering Europe for many years, that people protesting in France is not, shall we say, unusual.
sentences.zh: Mark，我们都知道，而且你作为多年报道欧洲的记者也知道，在法国，人们抗议并不是什么稀罕事。

sentences.en: But tell us why this time is different.
sentences.zh: 但请告诉我们，为什么这次有所不同？

sentences.en: First of all, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 首先，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: The French have a lot of muscle memory when it comes to protesting.
sentences.zh: 法国人在抗议方面有着深厚的“肌肉记忆”。

sentences.en: This is a country in which protests are deeply ingrained in the culture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个抗议活动深深植根于其文化的国家。

sentences.en: But I think a couple of things are different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有几点不同之处。

sentences.en: One is the nature of the protesters.
sentences.zh: 首先是抗议者的性质。

sentences.en: They're really young.
sentences.zh: 他们非常年轻。

sentences.en: These are high school students, 14 to 17 years old, who are usually tomorrow's protesters.
sentences.zh: 这些是14到17岁的高中生，他们通常是未来的抗议者。

sentences.en: But in France, they are now today's protesters.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，他们现在成了当下的抗议者。

sentences.en: This is a movement that has started at high schools, outside of Paris initially, but spreading throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 这场运动最初始于巴黎以外的高中，但随后蔓延至全国。

sentences.en: And so that's one thing that's different about it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是不同之处之一。

sentences.en: What's also different is that these protests are occurring against a backdrop of multiple other crises in France.
sentences.zh: 另一个不同之处在于，这些抗议活动是在法国面临多重危机的背景下发生的。

sentences.en: So in addition to these protests over the state of France's education system, you've got port workers who have barricaded ports over the rising price of oil.
sentences.zh: 除了对法国教育体系现状的抗议外，还有港口工人因油价上涨而封锁港口。

sentences.en: You have public sector workers who are striking over pay freezes.
sentences.zh: 公共部门的员工因工资冻结而罢工。

sentences.en: And you have an evolving financial and economic crisis in the country that all goes back to a very simple but very difficult reality for France,
sentences.zh: 而且该国正在演变的金融和经济危机，这一切都归结为一个对法国来说既简单又困难的现实，

sentences.en: which is that this country can no longer afford its social welfare state.
sentences.zh: 那就是这个国家已经负担不起其社会福利制度了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the math just isn't adding up anymore, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来账目已经算不过来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And Mark, I think a lot of people know that France has a generous welfare state.
sentences.zh: Mark，我想很多人都知道法国拥有慷慨的福利制度。

sentences.en: But can you tell us specifically, what is costing the government so much money?
sentences.zh: 但你能具体告诉我们，是什么让政府花费了这么多钱吗？

sentences.en: Well, France, like a lot of European countries, offers very generous entitlements.
sentences.zh: 嗯，法国和许多欧洲国家一样，提供非常慷慨的福利。

sentences.en: They offer, you know, medical care.
sentences.zh: 他们提供医疗保健。

sentences.en: They offer free schooling.
sentences.zh: 他们提供免费教育。

sentences.en: They offer allowances to families.
sentences.zh: 他们向家庭提供津贴。

sentences.en: They offer a lot of paid leave for mothers, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们为母亲提供大量的带薪假期。

sentences.en: But what really sets France apart is its pension system.
sentences.zh: 但真正让法国与众不同的是它的养老金制度。

sentences.en: France has one of the lowest retirement ages of any European country.
sentences.zh: 法国拥有欧洲国家中最低的退休年龄之一。

sentences.en: It's currently just over 62 years.
sentences.zh: 目前刚过62岁。

sentences.en: And that allows French people to begin drawing on their pensions sooner than almost any of their European neighbors.
sentences.zh: 这使得法国人比几乎所有欧洲邻国都能更早地开始领取养老金。

sentences.en: And that saddles the French state with an enormous additional burden, one that even generous social welfare states like Germany, for example, don't have.
sentences.zh: 这给法国政府带来了巨大的额外负担，即使是像德国这样慷慨的福利国家也没有这种负担。

sentences.en: Yeah, all the benefits you were talking about sound pretty great.
sentences.zh: 是的，你提到的所有福利听起来都很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, I know a lot of Americans would be totally jealous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道很多美国人会非常嫉妒。

sentences.en: But it also sounds pretty expensive.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来也相当昂贵。

sentences.en: Yeah, and expensive is actually an understatement.
sentences.zh: 是的，用“昂贵”来形容其实都算保守了。

sentences.en: So France has been living beyond its means for something like 20 years now.
sentences.zh: 法国已经入不敷出大约20年了。

sentences.en: And as it has continued to increase its spending on social welfare, it has racked up some genuinely gargantuan debts.
sentences.zh: 随着它不断增加社会福利支出，它已经背负了极其庞大的债务。

sentences.en: Its total public debt is now larger than the gross domestic product of the country.
sentences.zh: 其公共债务总额现在已经超过了该国的国内生产总值。

sentences.en: And the government is running budget deficits that are greater than 5% of its GDP.
sentences.zh: 政府的预算赤字超过了其GDP的5%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Those numbers are also wildly at odds with the limits that France is supposed to meet as a member of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 这些数字也与法国作为欧盟成员国理应遵守的限制严重不符。

sentences.en: The European Union is a currency union.
sentences.zh: 欧盟是一个货币联盟。

sentences.en: And so when one country, particularly one as large as France and as central as France, to the European project is running unsustainable debts,
sentences.zh: 因此，当一个国家，特别是像法国这样对欧洲项目如此重要的大国，背负着不可持续的债务时，

sentences.en: it actually threatens the entire structure of the EU.
sentences.zh: 它实际上威胁到了整个欧盟的结构。

sentences.en: And so France's problems are not just France's alone.
sentences.zh: 所以法国的问题不仅仅是法国自己的问题。

sentences.en: They're also problems for its neighbors.
sentences.zh: 这也是其邻国的问题。

sentences.en: And this is a situation that Emmanuel Macron came into office nearly 10 years ago vowing to fix.
sentences.zh: 而这正是埃马纽埃尔·马克龙近10年前上任时誓言要解决的情况。

sentences.en: He came in as a former economics minister, a former investment banker, and he promised to do two things.
sentences.zh: 他作为前经济部长、前投资银行家上任，并承诺做两件事。

sentences.en: One, pass economic policies that rejuvenated the French economy, but also to be fiscally prudent, to try to balance France's books.
sentences.zh: 第一，通过振兴法国经济的经济政策；第二，保持财政审慎，试图平衡法国的账目。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's had almost a decade to follow through with this program.
sentences.zh: 他有近十年的时间来执行这个计划。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's in a way a story of unfulfilled promise.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某种程度上，这是一个未竟承诺的故事。

sentences.en: So when Macron came into office in 2017,
sentences.zh: 当马克龙在2017年上任时，

sentences.en: his promise was to try to reinvigorate the French economy, make France attractive again to investment, create an entrepreneurial culture.
sentences.zh: 他的承诺是试图重振法国经济，让法国重新吸引投资，创造一种创业文化。

sentences.en: And so among the things he did is he very controversially removed a tax on wealthy people.
sentences.zh: 因此，他所做的事情之一就是极具争议地取消了针对富人的税收。

sentences.en: He did labor market reform to try to make it easier for companies to lay off workers if they needed to.
sentences.zh: 他进行了劳动力市场改革，试图让企业在需要时更容易裁员。

sentences.en: And then most importantly, he tried to tackle France's pension system, most notably by raising the retirement age from 62 to 64.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他试图解决法国的养老金制度，最显著的就是将退休年龄从62岁提高到64岁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That pension reform fight in 2019 was killer for him.
sentences.zh: 2019年的那场养老金改革之战对他来说是致命的。

sentences.en: I mean, people were so angry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们非常愤怒。

sentences.en: I remember, you know, all these photos of people taking to the streets.
sentences.zh: 我记得人们走上街头的那些照片。

sentences.en: And it seemed like they were also really angry that at the same time as he was trying to cut benefits, he was also cutting taxes for the rich.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎他们也非常愤怒，因为在他试图削减福利的同时，他也在为富人减税。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think one of the problems that Macron had politically was that he became known as the president for the rich.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为马克龙在政治上面临的问题之一是他被称为“富人的总统”。

sentences.en: And that's a label that was very hard for him to shake and also became very damaging
sentences.zh: 这个标签让他很难摆脱，也变得非常有破坏性，

sentences.en: when there was a cost of living crisis and ordinary French people found their lives more difficult.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在生活成本危机爆发，普通法国人发现生活变得更加困难的时候。

sentences.en: But it is also worth noting that a couple of outside events in the world certainly got in his way.
sentences.zh: 但同样值得注意的是，世界上发生的几起外部事件确实阻碍了他。

sentences.en: A war broke out in Ukraine, which had a huge effect on energy prices and on inflation more generally.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰战争爆发，这对能源价格和整体通胀产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: He had to lead France through the COVID epidemic, which was very expensive for France as it was for every other government.
sentences.zh: 他必须带领法国度过新冠疫情，这对法国和所有其他政府来说都非常昂贵。

sentences.en: But then he was also thwarted by his own politics.
sentences.zh: 但随后他也受到了自身政治局势的阻碍。

sentences.en: Pension reform got bogged down.
sentences.zh: 养老金改革陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: It prompted a huge amount of proteSt.
sentences.zh: 它引发了大量的抗议。

sentences.en: In the end, the National Assembly decided to freeze the raise in retirement age.
sentences.zh: 最终，国民议会决定冻结退休年龄的提高。

sentences.en: And as his political situation deteriorated and his party lost its majority in the French parliament,
sentences.zh: 随着他的政治处境恶化，他的政党在法国议会失去了多数席位，

sentences.en: he basically kind of reverted to a muddling through strategy where he was merely throwing money at the problem.
sentences.zh: 他基本上退回到了“得过且过”的策略，仅仅是向问题砸钱。

sentences.en: And that's really where we find ourselves now, seven months before the end of his second term.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在所处的位置，距离他第二个任期结束还有七个月。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So he's throwing a lot of money at the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在向问题砸钱。

sentences.en: I mean, that's quite the journey from when he was running on fiscal responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这和他当初竞选时主张的财政责任相比，真是天差地别。

sentences.en: It is indeed a huge journey.
sentences.zh: 确实是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: And it's not one that's ending smoothly, by the way, because even as he sort of heads into the final lap of his presidency,
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是一个能顺利结束的过程，因为即使他进入了总统任期的最后阶段，

sentences.en: Macron is dealing with a couple other very expensive probleMs.
sentences.zh: 马克龙还在处理其他几个非常昂贵的问题。

sentences.en: One is the Iran war, which has, again, driven up the price of fuel and energy.
sentences.zh: 一个是伊朗战争，这再次推高了燃料和能源价格。

sentences.en: And the other is the pressure that Donald Trump has put on the NATO alliance since he returned to the White House.
sentences.zh: 另一个是唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫后对北约联盟施加的压力。

sentences.en: Trump is demanding that European countries pay a much greater share of the defense burden.
sentences.zh: 特朗普要求欧洲国家承担更大份额的国防负担。

sentences.en: And so that is something that is, of course, also reflected in increased government spending for the French government.
sentences.zh: 所以这当然也反映在法国政府增加的政府支出中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on top of all of that, because of the war in Iran, a lot of interest rates are staying high or even going higher, right?
sentences.zh: 而且最重要的是，由于伊朗战争，许多利率保持在高位甚至更高，对吧？

sentences.en: Which just piles on the pressure.
sentences.zh: 这只会加剧压力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that, in turn, has led to the latest crisis for the French, which is extreme volatility in the bond market.
sentences.zh: 而这反过来又导致了法国面临的最新危机，即债券市场的极端波动。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So bear with me for a second while I explain why this is important.
sentences.zh: 所以请耐心听我解释一下为什么这很重要。

sentences.en: Happy to bear with you, Mark.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意听你解释，Mark。

sentences.en: Bonds are a reflection of investors' confidence in the creditworthiness of a country.
sentences.zh: 债券反映了投资者对一个国家信誉的信心。

sentences.en: And the higher the yield, the higher the rate on a bond, the less faith investors have in a country's creditworthiness.
sentences.zh: 收益率越高，债券利率就越高，投资者对一个国家信誉的信心就越低。

sentences.en: What happened in France in the last week is that the yield on the 10-year French bond actually briefly went above 5%.
sentences.zh: 过去一周在法国发生的事情是，10年期法国国债的收益率实际上短暂超过了5%。

sentences.en: Which is commonly regarded as kind of the danger zone for bond market rates.
sentences.zh: 这通常被认为是债券市场利率的“危险区”。

sentences.en: And it makes it much more expensive for France to borrow money in the financial markets.
sentences.zh: 这使得法国在金融市场上借钱的成本变得高得多。

sentences.en: The reason this happened was complicated.
sentences.zh: 发生这种情况的原因很复杂。

sentences.en: It wasn't just a single event.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个单一事件。

sentences.en: Investors were looking at both the debt problem and the deficit problems we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 投资者同时关注着我们一直在谈论的债务问题和赤字问题。

sentences.en: They were also looking at these student protests and this prospect of spreading unrest around the country.
sentences.zh: 他们也在关注这些学生抗议活动以及全国范围内动荡蔓延的前景。

sentences.en: And lastly, they were adjusting to the reality that a far-right candidate, Marine Le Pen, might plausibly be elected president of France next year.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们正在适应一个现实，即极右翼候选人玛丽娜·勒庞明年可能当选法国总统。

sentences.en: And it was really these interlocking developments that the bond market and investors found so troubling.
sentences.zh: 正是这些相互交织的发展让债券市场和投资者感到如此不安。

sentences.en: So basically, all of it adds up to, like, Macron is about to leave office and it seems like the country is in a way worse place than when he started.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这一切加起来就像是马克龙即将离任，而国家似乎比他刚开始时处境更糟。

sentences.en: Well, I think sadly that there's some truth to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，遗憾的是，我认为这确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: I think Macron came in as a reformer hoping to really revitalize the French economy.
sentences.zh: 我认为马克龙上任时是一位改革者，希望能真正振兴法国经济。

sentences.en: He also came in as a centrist, a person who was going to govern pragmatically, almost in a post-partisan way,
sentences.zh: 他也是以中间派的身份上任的，一个打算务实执政的人，几乎是以一种超越党派的方式，

sentences.en: if you remember the way Barack Obama came into the White House in 2008.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得巴拉克·奥巴马2008年入主白宫的方式的话。

sentences.en: And President Macron would not like to hear this, but it's entirely possible that he leaves bequeathing France not only this very messy fiscal and financial picture,
sentences.zh: 马克龙总统可能不想听到这些，但完全有可能他留给法国的不仅是这幅非常混乱的财政和金融图景，

sentences.en: but also Emmanuel Macron may bequeath France its first post-war far-right government.
sentences.zh: 而且埃马纽埃尔·马克龙可能还会留给法国第一个战后极右翼政府。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wenna Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏版块中的《Connections》谜题，而且我非常喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游玩。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about Marine Le Pen.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来聊聊玛丽娜·勒庞。

sentences.en: A lot of people will know her as being this populist, anti-immigrant, anti-EU politician, but what's her approach to the economy?
sentences.zh: 很多人都知道她是一位民粹主义、反移民、反欧盟的政治家，但她在经济方面的主张是什么呢？

sentences.en: You know, so as you said, Vivian, Marine Le Pen is a populiSt.
sentences.zh: 如你所说，薇薇安，玛丽娜·勒庞确实是一位民粹主义者。

sentences.en: So she actually embraces economic policies that favor entitlements and that favor a large state role in the economy.
sentences.zh: 她实际上拥护那些支持福利保障、并主张国家在经济中发挥巨大作用的经济政策。

sentences.en: In fact, one of Le Pen's biggest promises going into this presidential election is to reduce France's retirement age from 64 back to 62.
sentences.zh: 事实上，勒庞在这次总统竞选中最大的承诺之一，就是将法国的退休年龄从64岁降回62岁。

sentences.en: Okay, so back to the status quo before Macron tried to reform it.
sentences.zh: 也就是回到马克龙试图改革之前的现状。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And of course, that's extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 当然，这极其昂贵。

sentences.en: It adds billions and billions of euros to France's pension burden.
sentences.zh: 这会给法国的养老金负担增加数百亿欧元的支出。

sentences.en: But what's sort of the great paradox here is that Marine Le Pen is running as a disruptor.
sentences.zh: 但这里最大的悖论在于，玛丽娜·勒庞是以颠覆者的身份参选的。

sentences.en: And yet, in a funny way, she's a bigger defender of the social welfare status quo in France than almost any other candidate for president.
sentences.zh: 然而有趣的是，在捍卫法国社会福利现状方面，她比几乎任何其他总统候选人都要坚定。

sentences.en: And that's perhaps the great contradiction about the far right in France.
sentences.zh: 这或许就是法国极右翼最大的矛盾所在。

sentences.en: Yeah, but maybe it shouldn't surprise us that a populist politician wants to prop up the social welfare benefits that people are used to.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但一位民粹主义政治家想要维持人们习以为常的社会福利待遇，这或许不该让我们感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I mean, right now, there are huge protests in the street over underfunded schools.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在街头正因学校资金不足而爆发大规模抗议。

sentences.en: So she probably doesn't want a repeat of what Macron faced in 2019 and 2023 when these massive protests erupted over his pension reform plan.
sentences.zh: 所以她可能不想重蹈马克龙在2019年和2023年面临的覆辙，当时他的养老金改革计划引发了大规模抗议。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a very valid observation.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常中肯的观察。

sentences.en: And it's probably why you haven't really heard any politician from the right, left,
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么你几乎没听到任何来自右翼、左翼

sentences.en: or center address these problems squarely and say that what France really needs is a period of painful fiscal belt tightening.
sentences.zh: 或中间派的政治家直面这些问题，并指出法国真正需要的是一段痛苦的财政紧缩时期。

sentences.en: And indeed, the other rising candidate in France is on the far left, a politician named Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who, by the way, is actively embracing the student's cause.
sentences.zh: 事实上，法国另一位崛起的候选人来自极左翼，名叫让-吕克·梅朗雄，顺便提一下，他正在积极支持学生运动。

sentences.en: He offers a prescription for fixing France's debt problems that is every bit as unrealistic as Marine Le Pen's, just in a different way.
sentences.zh: 他为解决法国债务问题开出的药方，和玛丽娜·勒庞的一样不切实际，只是方式不同而已。

sentences.en: What Mélenchon wants to do is simply cancel a large chunk of France's debt.
sentences.zh: 梅朗雄想做的仅仅是取消法国很大一部分债务。

sentences.en: You can just cancel it?
sentences.zh: 可以直接取消吗？

sentences.en: Well, you can't, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然不能。

sentences.en: You can threaten to cancel it.
sentences.zh: 你可以威胁要取消它。

sentences.en: But the moment you do that, you sow chaos in the market.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你这么做，就会在市场上播下混乱的种子。

sentences.en: You cause a giant crisis at the heart of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 你会引发一场欧盟核心地带的巨大危机。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So really, it's not a credible remedy, but to a segment of France's angry voters, it probably sounds like the kind of medicine they'd like to have.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实不是一个可靠的补救措施，但对于一部分愤怒的法国选民来说，这听起来可能正是他们想要的“良药”。

sentences.en: So this is where France finds itself, with a political establishment that is really not in any way facing up squarely to the problems that they need to deal with.
sentences.zh: 这就是法国目前的处境，政治体制内的人根本没有直面他们需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: Okay, so looking at the leading candidates in the French election, the odds of getting a more financially credible government after the election are pretty low, sounds like.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么纵观法国大选的领先候选人，选举后出现一个财政上更可靠的政府的可能性听起来很低。

sentences.en: And if you're an investor, you're worried that France is not going to be creditworthy at all.
sentences.zh: 如果你是投资者，你会担心法国根本不具备偿债能力。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And it leads you to some fairly dark paths.
sentences.zh: 这会把你引向一些相当黑暗的道路。

sentences.en: I think people in Europe these days are recalling the Greek debt crisis, which happened in the late aughts when the Greek government got itself into terrible trouble,
sentences.zh: 我想如今欧洲人都在回想希腊债务危机，那发生在2000年代末，当时希腊政府陷入了可怕的困境，

sentences.en: mismanaged its budget, racked up debt, and eventually had to be bailed out by the European Central Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
sentences.zh: 预算管理不善，债台高筑，最终不得不由欧洲央行和国际货币基金组织进行救助。

sentences.en: After years of very difficult and sometimes bitter negotiations between Athens and Brussels, a lot of other members of the EU, notably Germany,
sentences.zh: 在雅典和布鲁塞尔之间经历了多年极其艰难甚至痛苦的谈判后，许多其他欧盟成员国，特别是德国，

sentences.en: where I think German voters were very bitter at being asked to pick up the cost of Greece's free spending ways.
sentences.zh: 我想德国选民对于被要求为希腊的挥霍买单感到非常愤慨。

sentences.en: Now, just imagine that scenario unfolding with France, a much, much bigger economy at the center of the EU, and a country, by the way,
sentences.zh: 现在，试想一下如果这种情况发生在法国，一个处于欧盟中心、经济规模大得多的国家，而且顺便提一下，

sentences.en: that is going in the wrong direction fiscally.
sentences.zh: 这个国家在财政上正走向错误的方向。

sentences.en: The Greeks were only able to get these bailouts by agreeing to these very austere budgets with heavy-duty budget cuts.
sentences.zh: 希腊人只有在同意实施极其严苛的预算和大幅削减开支的情况下，才获得了这些救助。

sentences.en: French politicians are actually proposing to spend more.
sentences.zh: 而法国政治家们实际上提议的是增加支出。

sentences.en: So you can imagine the bitterness that might arise in other European countries if they now are on the hook for France's debts at a time when the French are actually talking about spending even more money.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，如果其他欧洲国家现在要为法国的债务买单，而法国人却在谈论花更多的钱，这会引发多大的愤慨。

sentences.en: This could pose a genuine threat to European unity.
sentences.zh: 这可能会对欧洲的团结构成真正的威胁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I do want to say at this point, just to be clear, we're in early days of this crisis.
sentences.zh: 但我现在想说明一点，我们要清楚，这场危机还处于早期阶段。

sentences.en: I think that things would have to get a good deal worse for us to be talking about a bailout by the European Central Bank.
sentences.zh: 我认为情况必须变得糟糕得多，我们才会谈论欧洲央行的救助。

sentences.en: But the mere fact that this has begun to enter the conversation is already a pretty alarming indicator about the state of France's finances.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅是这一点开始进入讨论范畴，就已经是一个关于法国财政状况的相当惊人的指标了。

sentences.en: And I guess the difference is that France is so much more economically important than Greece.
sentences.zh: 我想区别在于，法国在经济上的重要性远超希腊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: France is Europe's second largest economy.
sentences.zh: 法国是欧洲第二大经济体。

sentences.en: France is one of the original founders of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 法国是欧盟的创始国之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: France is actually the only nuclear-armed state in the European Union.
sentences.zh: 法国实际上是欧盟中唯一的拥核国家。

sentences.en: So for a whole variety of reasons, both economically and politically, France falling into financial distress is just of a completely different magnitude than Greece or, honestly,
sentences.zh: 所以出于各种原因，无论是经济上还是政治上，法国陷入财政困境的严重程度完全不同于希腊，或者说，老实讲，

sentences.en: several of the other southern European countries that have skirted up against financial distress in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 不同于过去曾徘徊在财政困境边缘的其他几个南欧国家。

sentences.en: It sounds like for the rest of Europe, France is kind of too big to fail.
sentences.zh: 听起来对于欧洲其他国家来说，法国属于“大到不能倒”。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I'm just thinking ahead to the presidential election next year.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我正在展望明年的总统大选。

sentences.en: France may end up with a president, Marine Le Pen, who has made very clear that she opposes the EU.
sentences.zh: 法国最终可能会选出一位明确反对欧盟的总统——玛丽娜·勒庞。

sentences.en: So how would that work if you have a French president who opposes the EU, but Europe is being asked to bail out France?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果一位法国总统反对欧盟，而欧洲又被要求救助法国，这该如何运作呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Marine Le Pen used to favor France leaving the European Union.
sentences.zh: 嗯，玛丽娜·勒庞过去曾支持法国退出欧盟。

sentences.en: She shelved the idea of Frexit, which is what it was once known as, a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 几年前，她搁置了“脱法”（Frexit）的想法，也就是当时所称的那个概念。

sentences.en: But the fact of the matter is, one of the areas where Marine Le Pen does see a major opportunity to cut spending is in France's contribution to the European Commission.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，玛丽娜·勒庞确实认为削减开支的一个主要机会在于法国对欧盟委员会的贡献。

sentences.en: So not only might the EU be on the hook for bailing out France, but they might also be getting less money from France.
sentences.zh: 所以，欧盟不仅可能要为救助法国买单，他们从法国那里得到的钱可能还会变少。

sentences.en: And for that reason, this poses yet another threat to kind of the harmony of the European project.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，这又对欧洲一体化进程的和谐构成了另一种威胁。

sentences.en: Well, like you said, France is not Greece.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像你说的，法国不是希腊。

sentences.en: It's a lot bigger.
sentences.zh: 它大得多。

sentences.en: Saving it would put huge strain on the other EU countries.
sentences.zh: 拯救它会给其他欧盟国家带来巨大的压力。

sentences.en: Might it be too big to save?
sentences.zh: 它会不会大到无法拯救？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: You could probably argue that both ways.
sentences.zh: 你可能可以从两个方面来辩论。

sentences.en: You could argue that France is too big to fail because it's such a central player in the European Union.
sentences.zh: 你可以说法国大到不能倒，因为它是欧盟的核心参与者。

sentences.en: But you might also argue that it's too big to save because these pension obligations, particularly if the retirement age is lowered the way Marine Le Pen would like it to be,
sentences.zh: 但你也可以说它大到无法拯救，因为这些养老金义务，特别是如果按照玛丽娜·勒庞希望的那样降低退休年龄，

sentences.en: could make the bill here simply unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 可能会让这笔账单变得根本无法承受。

sentences.en: And at a time when a lot of these other European countries are dealing with their own economic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而且是在许多其他欧洲国家都在处理自身经济问题的时候。

sentences.en: Germany is in a much more parlous situation now than it was in 2009, 2010 when it had to come to the aid of Greece.
sentences.zh: 德国现在的处境比2009年、2010年不得不援助希腊时要危险得多。

sentences.en: So these are countries that are dealing with political headwinds.
sentences.zh: 所以这些国家正面临着政治上的逆风。

sentences.en: They're dealing with their own rising populist parties and their own slow-growing economies and worsening fiscal situations.
sentences.zh: 他们正在应对自己国内崛起的民粹主义政党、增长缓慢的经济以及不断恶化的财政状况。

sentences.en: So this is sort of precisely the wrong moment that you would ask European countries to ante up to bail out a country as big as France.
sentences.zh: 所以，这恰恰是要求欧洲国家掏钱去救助像法国这么大国家的错误时机。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So is it just inevitable now that a bailout is what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，现在救助是否已经不可避免了？

sentences.en: Because they don't really have other solutions, do they?
sentences.zh: 因为他们真的没有其他解决办法了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's very hard to contemplate France not being bailed out if it ever came to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果真到了那一步，很难想象法国不会被救助。

sentences.en: The French are in the process of negotiating a new budget and they may get it through.
sentences.zh: 法国人正在协商一项新预算，他们可能会通过。

sentences.en: But it's not clear that even if they did, it would solve their problem.
sentences.zh: 但不清楚即使通过了，能否解决他们的问题。

sentences.en: And so for right now, their best option is to hope that eventually a solution will be found in Iran, that energy prices, oil and gas prices will come back to Earth,
sentences.zh: 所以目前，他们最好的选择是寄希望于最终能找到解决伊朗问题的办法，能源价格、石油和天然气价格能回落，

sentences.en: and that France will continue to be able to muddle through.
sentences.zh: 并且法国能继续勉强维持下去。

sentences.en: That's an awfully slender reed to hang everything on, but I think that's roughly where we are right now.
sentences.zh: 把一切都寄托在如此脆弱的希望上，但这大概就是我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: Yeah, it strikes me, Mark, that a lot of what you're talking about here is familiar to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，马克，我感觉到你在这里谈论的很多内容对美国来说都很熟悉。

sentences.en: We also have a huge debt load.
sentences.zh: 我们也背负着巨大的债务负担。

sentences.en: There are also investor worries about whether the U.S.
sentences.zh: 投资者也担心美国

sentences.en: government is capable of ever getting to a place where we have less debt.
sentences.zh: 政府是否有能力达到债务减少的境地。

sentences.en: So draw that out for me a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，请为我详细分析一下这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: There are a lot of similarities, not least high rates on U.S.
sentences.zh: 有很多相似之处，尤其是美国国债的高利率。

sentences.en: treasuries.
sentences.zh: 然而，美国和法国之间有一个巨大的区别，那就是美国

sentences.en: However, there's one big difference between the United States and France, and that is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 可以不断印钞，并真正通过扩张经济和货币供应来摆脱这些问题，而作为欧洲货币联盟成员的法国却做不到。

sentences.en: can keep printing money and can really expand its economy, its money supply out of these problems in a way that France, as a member of the European Monetary Union, can't do.
sentences.zh: 所以美国

sentences.en: So the U.S.
sentences.zh: 拥有法国所不具备的机动空间，这也就引出了关于法国被邻国救助的讨论。

sentences.en: has a freedom of maneuver that France does not have, and that then leads you to these discussions of France being bailed out by its neighbors.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 那么，现在是不是法国终于要正视一方面资助社会福利，

sentences.en: So is this the moment where France is finally going to reckon with the total tension between funding social welfare on the one hand
sentences.zh: 另一方面却缺乏资金来维持这种平衡之间的巨大张力的时刻了？

sentences.en: and the lack of money to do it on the other hand?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着法国福利制度的终结？

sentences.en: Like, is this kind of the end of the welfare system in France?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这正是每个人都在问的问题。

sentences.en: Yes, that's the question I think everybody is asking.
sentences.zh: 我认为法国人的本能，就像过去20年左右一样，将是继续勉强维持。

sentences.en: And I think the French instinct, as it has been for the last 20 years or so, will be to continue to muddle through.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，除非法国能得到一些极其幸运的转机，比如乌克兰和伊朗战争的迅速结束，石油和天然气价格的突然下跌。

sentences.en: But remember, unless France gets some extremely lucky breaks, a quick end to the war in Ukraine and Iran, a sudden drop in the price of oil and gas.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们必须非常幸运才行。

sentences.en: Yeah, they'd have to get very lucky.
sentences.zh: 他们必须非常幸运。

sentences.en: They'd have to get very lucky.
sentences.zh: 他们不太可能做到。

sentences.en: They're not likely to.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为他们将不得不面对这些非常、非常困难的问题。

sentences.en: And as a result, I think they will have to confront these very, very difficult questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你思考一下法国正在发生的事情，政府正在花费巨额资金来资助老年人的养老金，

sentences.en: So if you think about what's happening in France, the government is spending an extraordinary amount of money to fund the pensions of older people,
sentences.zh: 这剥夺了它在年轻人、年轻家庭和普通法国工人身上投入资源的财力。

sentences.en: depriving it of the resources to spend money on young people, on young families, on ordinary French workers.
sentences.zh: 所以本周人们提出的另一个问题是，这些学生抗议活动是否会扩大到包括经济中许多其他部门的人，
